speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant presenting with recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing, particularly during specific activities. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me exactly what those specific activities are?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The clinical presentation of stridor and wheezing exacerbated by neck flexion, crying, and feeding, combined with post-prandial vomiting, is classic for this condition. No further tests are required for this diagnosis.
